PLANNING AND ZONING RECOMMENDATION:  
 
The Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission has recommended approval of the Special Use 
Permit on APN 110-07-001H to the Navajo County Board of Supervisors, subject to the following 
conditions: 
 
1. This Special Use Permit shall allow for the installation of a meteorological tower, with a 
maximum height of 197 feet. 
 
2. The meteorological tower shall be e rected only in the location indicated on the approved site 
plan, except as may otherwise be approved by the Navajo County Public Works Department. 
 
3. Building permits are required for the meteorological tower and any accessory uses.  Any 
required permits shall be obtained prior to construction. 
 
4. A Floodplain Use Permit, if required, shall be obtained prior to issuance of any building permits. 
 
5. The meteorological tower foundation and all guy-wire footings shall be enclosed by a security 
fence with a maximum height of 7 feet (excluding barbed wire or cyclone wire).  Information 
regarding who to contact in the event of an emergency or any problems with the tower or its 
associated uses and structures shall be placed upon the fence.  The information shal l include a 
contact name, company name, and phone number for someone who can be reached 24 hours a 
day, 7 days a week. 
 
6. The meteorological tower shall include the installation of low-intensity, red blinking lighting for 
night-time visibility that conforms to FAA and FCC regulations.  The use of strobes or strobe -
type lighting is prohibited.  The meteorological tower shall also be painted in conformance with 
FAA and FCC requirements.

<!-- page 687 -->
7. Prior to acquiring a building permit, t he applicant shall work with the Arizona Game and Fish 
Department to design their tower in order to comply with the following requirements: 
 
a. Install Bird Flight Diverters (BFDs) at regular intervals along the full length of all outer 
meteorological tower guy wires. 
b. Install Aircraft Warning Markers (AWMs) near the tops of all outer meteorological 
tower guy wires. 
c. Paint the top of the meteorological tower orange and white. 
d. Locate the meteorological tower away from cliffs, canyons, water sources, and other 
wildlife-attracting features to the fullest extent possible. 
 
8. The applicant shall provide GPS locations of the final site of the meteorological tower to the 
Arizona Game and Fish Department, and to the Navajo County Public Works Department. 
 
9. The meteorological tower shall be located so that it will not fall onto an adjacent property nor 
another structure in case of failure. 
 
10. Prior to issuance of any building permits for the meteorological tower, the developer shall submit 
to the Navajo County Public Works Department information regarding the manufacturer of the 
tower, structural information, and information regarding who to contact in the event of an 
emergency or any problems with the tower. 
 
11. If the permitted Special Use is not utilized within a twenty-four (24) month period from the date 
of approval by the Board of Supervisors, this permit shall become null and void. 
 
12. Development and use of the site shall includ e efforts, consistent with Best Management 
Practices, to reduce and mitigate dust created by this project.  Efforts shall also be made to 
reduce the removal of vegetation during construction and use of the site and any roadways that 
provide access to the s ite.  Upon the removal of the meteorological tower and associated 
structures, the site and any roadways that provide access to the site shall be restored and re -
vegetated to their pre-disturbed/native condition by the applicant. 
 
13. Within six (6) months after the tower ceases to be used, the applicant, at their sole expense, shall 
remove the tower and any accessories from the site. 
 
14. This Special Use Permit and the rights granted herein shall expire sixty (60) months (5 years) 
from the issuance of a Certificate of Occupancy (C.O.O.), unless an extension is granted by the 
Board of Supervisors upon a recommendation by the Planning & Zoni ng Commission.  
Application for an extension shall be made no later than 90 days before the date of expiration.  
If timely application is made, the expiration shall be tolled until a final decision by the Board of 
Supervisors.

Dear   Mr.   Wynn:   
  
The  Arizona  Game  and  Fish  Department  (Department)  has  reviewed  the  proposed  installation  of               
five  meteorological  monitoring  towers  (MET  towers)  by  Pattern  Renewables  Development            
Company  2  LLC  (Pattern)  on  five  privately-owned  parcels  approximately  8.5  to  16.5  miles               
southwest  of  Holbrook,  Arizona  in  unincorporated  Navajo  County,  Arizona.  It  is  the              
Department’s  understanding  that  Pattern’s  proposed  installation  of  meteorological  test  towers  is             
part   of   a   larger   project   to   explore   and   potentially   develop   wind   resources   in   this   area.     
  
Under  Title  17  of  the  Arizona  Revised  Statutes,  the  Department,  by  and  through  the  Arizona                 
Game  and  Fish  Commission  (Commission),  has  jurisdictional  authority  and  public  trust             
responsibilities  for  management  of  the  state's  fish  and  wildlife  resources.  It  is  the  mission  of  the                  
Department  to  conserve  and  protect  Arizona’s  diverse  fish  and  wildlife  resources  and  manage  for                
safe,  compatible  outdoor  recreation  opportunities  for  current  and  future  generations.  Similarly,             
the  Department  recognizes  the  importance  of  planning  efforts  that  contribute  to  regional  and  the                
state’s  economic  growth  needs  and  opportunities  to  develop  renewable  energy  locations.  The              
Department  recognizes  that  appropriate  coordination,  proper  planning,  and  voluntary           
implementation  of  best  management  practices  allow  projects  to  be  developed  that  avoid,              
minimize,   or   mitigate   potential   impacts   to   wildlife   habitat   and   populations.     
  
The  Department  supports  the  development  of  wind  energy  as  a  source  of  clean  and  renewable                 
energy  and  believes  that  with  proper  placement  and  planning  the  benefits  of  wind  energy                
outweigh  the  potential  negative  effects  to  wildlife  populations.  As  identified  in  the  Department's               
" GUIDELINES  FOR  REDUCING  IMPACTS  TO  WILDLIFE  FROM  WIND  ENERGY           
DEVELOPMENT  IN  ARIZONA ”  ( Guidelines ),  primary  concerns  with  MET  towers  are  the             
potential  for  avian  and  bats  mortality  due  to  collisions  with  tower  guy-wires.  Another  potential                
issue  from  unmarked  towers  and  guy-wires  concerns  risk  to  Department  pilots  engaged  in               
low-altitude  wildlife  survey  flights  due  to  the  towers'  lack  of  visibility  from  the  air.  The                 
Department  appreciates  Pattern's  implementation  of  the  Department's  guidelines  to  minimize            
impacts  to  wildlife  and  risk  to  our  pilots.  To  further  protect  our  pilots,  the  Department  would  like                   
to  be  able  to  incorporate  the  GPS  coordinates  of  all  final  met  tower  locations  into  a  database  our                    
pilots  use  to  avoid  hazards.  Please  notify  the  Department  when  the  towers  are  erected  and  when

<!-- page 711 -->

they  are  taken  down  so  the  database  can  be  updated.  If  the  project  progresses,  the  Department                  
would  like  to  be  involved  in  the  planning/review  of  survey  designs,  provide  input  on  developing                 
best-management   practices,   and   post-construction   monitoring.   
  
The  Department  appreciates  Pattern’s  early  coordination  and  looks  forward  to  working             
proactively  and  collaboratively  to  develop  this  economically-important  facility  while  also            
minimizing  any  impacts  to  wildlife  during  development  and  operation  of  the  facility,  if  this

PUBLIC HEARING: Consideration and possible adoption of Resolution Number 14-2021
approving/denying a Special Use Permit to construct and operate a 60 meter (approx. 197 foot)
meteorological tower on APN 110-01-001C, a portion of Township 15 North, Range 19 East,
Section 15 of the Gila and Salt River Meridian.
Background:
The proposed project is a 60 meter (approximately 197 foot) meteorological tower.  The applicant
is intending to use the tower to record meteorological conditions to research for a potential future
electrical generation project.
The applicant for this project intends to have this tower constructed within a 2-year period and is
requesting a period of at least 5 years to operate the tower and collect data.  
None of the structures and equipment on the site will be permanent.  Once site usage has
terminated, all of these structures and equipment will be removed and the site will be restored to
previous conditions.  
This item was unanimously recommended for approval at the Planning and Zoning Commission
meeting held on February 18, 2021, subject to conditions outlined in the Staff Report and
Resolution for Approval.  These conditions included an amended version of condition five (5),
which was recommended to be amended to state that fencing would only be necessary around
footings of the guy-wires and the foundation of the tower, as opposed to the entirety of the site.
Recommendation: 
Staff and the Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission recommend approval of the
Special Use Permit, subject to the conditions within the Staff Report.

BACKGROUND/PROJECT DESCRIPTION:  
 
The applicant is requesting Special Use Permit s to allow for the construction and operation of  five (5) 
different, 60 meter (approximately 197 foot) meteorological towers.  The location of the meteorological 
towers ranges from approximately 8.5 miles to 16.5 miles to the southwest of Holbrook. The applicant 
intends to use these towers to record met eorological conditions to research for a potential future 
electrical generation project. 
 
As far as construction of the towers, the applicant has described them as, “constructed of a guyed steel

<!-- page 716 -->
monopole structure approximately 60 meters tall.  Each structure would be installed within a cleared, 
approximately 0.03 -acre pad, and would occupy app roximately 2 acres when including the area 
encompassing the guy-wires.  For maximum safety, the towers would be painted orange and aviation 
white and include balls on the guy -wires.  To protect wildlife, bird flight diverters will be installed on 
all MET tower guy-wires at spaced intervals and towers are not located near wildlife attracting features 
(i.e. cliffs, canyons, water sources).” 
 
The applicant is planning to phase their installation of towers over a 2-year period from approval of the 
Special Use Permits.  In the applicant’s narrative, it has been noted that there is a request of a 5 -year 
operation period for these towers. 
 
The applicants will access these tower locations via State Route 377 and existing roadways that branch 
off to the locations. 
 
None of the structures and equipment on the sites will be permanent and will be removed from the site 
once usage has terminated.  The site will be required to be restored to the pre -disturbed/native state to 
the greatest extent possible upon completion of the usage of the meteorological tower. 
 
The applicant has reached out to the Arizona Game and Fish Department regarding these projects and 
Staff has been included within these interactions.  As of February 11th, 2021, no official letter has been 
received fr om the Arizona Game and Fish Department regarding conditions.  The Game and Fish 
Department has confirmed that they will have an official response to Staff prior to the scheduled 
Planning and Zoning Commission meeting on February 11th, 2021.  Staff has based conditions from the 
Game and Fish Department upon historical requests from this agency, which have been the same for all 
researched projects of this nature.  If the letter provides any new or changed conditions that are requested 
from Game and Fish, Sta ff will make sure to note this and change their official recommendation to 
reflect the alterations.  The typical conditions requested from Game and Fish, which have been included 
in Staff recommendations, are as follows: 
 
“To minimize collision risks to birds, bats, and Department personnel, the Department sees great benefit 
to MET tower construction by implementing the following measures: 
1. Install Bird Flight Diverters (BFDs) at regular intervals along the full length of all outer met 
tower guy wires to increase visibility of wires to birds. 
2. Install Aircraft Warning Markers (AWMs) near the tops of all outer met tower guy wires to 
increase visibility to pilots. 
3. Paint the tops of all met towers orange and white to increase visibility to pilots. 
4. Provide the Department with GPS coordinates of all final met tower locations. 
5. Locate MET towers away from cliffs, canyons, water sources, and other wildlife -attracting 
features to the fullest extent possible.” 
 
At the February 18, 2021 Planning and Zoning Commission meeting, all five of the meteorological 
towers were unanimously recommended for approval, provided that condition five (5) be amended to 
state fencing would only be necessary around footings of the guy-wires and the foundation of the tower 
and that the term of the Special Use Permits not exceed five (5) years.  Condition five has been amended 
to reflect this recommendation.  As there was already a recommendation for a five (5) year Special Use 
Permit term, condition fourteen (14) remains the same.  There were discussions regarding condition six 
(6) and lighting.  It was clarified that this condition only takes effect if lighting is required per FAA 
standards.

February   16,   2021  
  
Mr.   Allen   Wynn   
Pattern   Renewables   Development   Company   2   LLC   
1088   Sansome   Street   
San   Francisco,   CA   94111   
  
RE:   Hot   Air   Wind   MET   Tower   Project     
  
Dear   Mr.   Wynn:   
  
The  Arizona  Game  and  Fish  Department  (Department)  has  reviewed  the  proposed  installation  of               
five  meteorological  monitoring  towers  (MET  towers)  by  Pattern  Renewables  Development            
Company  2  LLC  (Pattern)  on  five  privately-owned  parcels  approximately  8.5  to  16.5  miles               
southwest  of  Holbrook,  Arizona  in  unincorporated  Navajo  County,  Arizona.  It  is  the              
Department’s  understanding  that  Pattern’s  proposed  installation  of  meteorological  test  towers  is             
part   of   a   larger   project   to   explore   and   potentially   develop   wind   resources   in   this   area.     
  
Under  Title  17  of  the  Arizona  Revised  Statutes,  the  Department,  by  and  through  the  Arizona                 
Game  and  Fish  Commission  (Commission),  has  jurisdictional  authority  and  public  trust             
responsibilities  for  management  of  the  state's  fish  and  wildlife  resources.  It  is  the  mission  of  the                  
Department  to  conserve  and  protect  Arizona’s  diverse  fish  and  wildlife  resources  and  manage  for                
safe,  compatible  outdoor  recreation  opportunities  for  current  and  future  generations.  Similarly,             
the  Department  recognizes  the  importance  of  planning  efforts  that  contribute  to  regional  and  the                
state’s  economic  growth  needs  and  opportunities  to  develop  renewable  energy  locations.  The              
Department  recognizes  that  appropriate  coordination,  proper  planning,  and  voluntary           
implementation  of  best  management  practices  allow  projects  to  be  developed  that  avoid,              
minimize,   or   mitigate   potential   impacts   to   wildlife   habitat   and   populations.     
  
The  Department  supports  the  development  of  wind  energy  as  a  source  of  clean  and  renewable                 
energy  and  believes  that  with  proper  placement  and  planning  the  benefits  of  wind  energy                
outweigh  the  potential  negative  effects  to  wildlife  populations.  As  identified  in  the  Department's               
" GUIDELINES  FOR  REDUCING  IMPACTS  TO  WILDLIFE  FROM  WIND  ENERGY           
DEVELOPMENT  IN  ARIZONA ”  ( Guidelines ),  primary  concerns  with  MET  towers  are  the             
potential  for  avian  and  bats  mortality  due  to  collisions  with  tower  guy-wires.  Another  potential                
issue  from  unmarked  towers  and  guy-wires  concerns  risk  to  Department  pilots  engaged  in               
low-altitude  wildlife  survey  flights  due  to  the  towers'  lack  of  visibility  from  the  air.  The                 
Department  appreciates  Pattern's  implementation  of  the  Department's  guidelines  to  minimize            
impacts  to  wildlife  and  risk  to  our  pilots.  To  further  protect  our  pilots,  the  Department  would  like                   
to  be  able  to  incorporate  the  GPS  coordinates  of  all  final  met  tower  locations  into  a  database  our                    
pilots  use  to  avoid  hazards.  Please  notify  the  Department  when  the  towers  are  erected  and  when

<!-- page 743 -->
Hot   Air   Wind   MET   Tower   Project   
February   16,   2021   
Page   2   of   2   
they  are  taken  down  so  the  database  can  be  updated.  If  the  project  progresses,  the  Department                  
would  like  to  be  involved  in  the  planning/review  of  survey  designs,  provide  input  on  developing                 
best-management   practices,   and   post-construction   monitoring.   
  
The  Department  appreciates  Pattern’s  early  coordination  and  looks  forward  to  working             
proactively  and  collaboratively  to  develop  this  economically-important  facility  while  also            
minimizing  any  impacts  to  wildlife  during  development  and  operation  of  the  facility,  if  this                
project  does  move  forward.  Please  contact  me  at  623-236-7222  or   ACavalcant@azgfd.gov  if  you               
have   any   questions,   or   would   like   to   further   discuss   our   concerns   and   recommendations.

Board of Supervisors Regular 8. e.        
Meeting Date: 04/13/2021  
Title: Hot Air Wind Met Towers MET Tower #4 - District III - SUP
Submitted For: Berrin Nejad, Community Development Director 
Submitted By: Cody Cooper, Planner II
Department: Public Works Division: Planning & Zoning
Presented By: Cody Cooper
Motion before the Board:
PUBLIC HEARING: Consideration and possible adoption of Resolution Number 15-2021
approving/denying a Special Use Permit to construct and operate a 60 meter (approx. 197 foot)
meteorological tower on APN 110-06-002A, a portion of Township 16 North, Range 19 East,
Section 12 of the Gila and Salt River Meridian.
Background:
The proposed project is a 60 meter (approximately 197 foot) meteorological tower.  The applicant
is intending to use the tower to record meteorological conditions to research for a potential future
electrical generation project.  
The applicant for this project intends to have this tower constructed within a 2-year period and is
requesting a period of at least 5 years to operate the tower and collect data.  
None of the structures and equipment on the site will be permanent.  Once site usage has
terminated, all of these structures and equipment will be removed and the site will be restored to
previous conditions. 
This item was unanimously recommended for approval at the Planning and Zoning Commission
meeting held on February 18, 2021, subject to conditions outlined in the Staff Report and
Resolution for Approval.  These conditions included an amended version of condition five (5),
which was recommended to be amended to state that fencing would only be necessary around
footings of the guy-wires and the foundation of the tower, as opposed to the entirety of the site.
Recommendation: 
Staff and the Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission recommend approval of the
Special Use Permit, subject to the conditions within the Staff Report.

BACKGROUND/PROJECT DESCRIPTION:  
 
The applicant is requesting Special Use Permit s to allow for the construction and operation of  five (5) 
different, 60 meter (approximately 197 foot) meteorological towers.  The location of the meteorological 
towers ranges from approximately 8.5 miles to 16.5 miles to the southwest of Holbrook. The applicant 
intends to use these towers to record met eorological conditions to research for a potential future 
electrical generation project. 
 
As far as construction of the towers, the applicant has described them as, “constructed of a guyed steel

<!-- page 748 -->
monopole structure approximately 60 meters tall.  Each structure would be installed within a cleared, 
approximately 0.03 -acre pad, and would occupy app roximately 2 acres when including the area 
encompassing the guy-wires.  For maximum safety, the towers would be painted orange and aviation 
white and include balls on the guy -wires.  To protect wildlife, bird flight diverters will be installed on 
all MET tower guy-wires at spaced intervals and towers are not located near wildlife attracting features 
(i.e. cliffs, canyons, water sources).” 
 
The applicant is planning to phase their installation of towers over a 2-year period from approval of the 
Special Use Permits.  In the applicant’s narrative, it has been noted that there is a request of a 5 -year 
operation period for these towers. 
 
The applicants will access these tower locations via State Route 377 and existing roadways that branch 
off to the locations. 
 
None of the structures and equipment on the sites will be permanent and will be removed from the site 
once usage has terminated.  The site will be required to be restored to the pre -disturbed/native state to 
the greatest extent possible upon completion of the usage of the meteorological tower. 
 
The applicant has reached out to the Arizona Game and Fish Department regarding these projects and 
Staff has been included within these interactions.  As of February 11th, 2021, no official letter has been 
received fr om the Arizona Game and Fish Department regarding conditions.  The Game and Fish 
Department has confirmed that they will have an official response to Staff prior to the scheduled 
Planning and Zoning Commission meeting on February 11th, 2021.  Staff has based conditions from the 
Game and Fish Department upon historical requests from this agency, which have been the same for all 
researched projects of this nature.  If the letter provides any new or changed conditions that are requested 
from Game and Fish, Sta ff will make sure to note this and change their official recommendation to 
reflect the alterations.  The typical conditions requested from Game and Fish, which have been included 
in Staff recommendations, are as follows: 
 
“To minimize collision risks to birds, bats, and Department personnel, the Department sees great benefit 
to MET tower construction by implementing the following measures: 
1. Install Bird Flight Diverters (BFDs) at regular intervals along the full length of all outer met 
tower guy wires to increase visibility of wires to birds. 
2. Install Aircraft Warning Markers (AWMs) near the tops of all outer met tower guy wires to 
increase visibility to pilots. 
3. Paint the tops of all met towers orange and white to increase visibility to pilots. 
4. Provide the Department with GPS coordinates of all final met tower locations. 
5. Locate MET towers away from cliffs, canyons, water sources, and other wildlife -attracting 
features to the fullest extent possible.” 
 
At the February 18, 2021 Planning and Zoning Commission meeting, all five of the meteorological 
towers were unanimously recommended for approval, provided that condition five (5) be amended to 
state fencing would only be necessary around footings of the guy-wires and the foundation of the tower 
and that the term of the Special Use Permits not exceed five (5) years.  Condition five has been amended 
to reflect this recommendation.  As there was already a recommendation for a five (5) year Special Use 
Permit term, condition fourteen (14) remains the same.  There were discussions regarding condition six 
(6) and lighting.  It was clarified that this condition only takes effect if lighting is required per FAA 
standards.

PLANNING AND ZONING RECOMMENDATION:  
 
The Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission has recommended approval of the Special Use 
Permit on APN 110-07-001H to the Navajo County Board of Supervisors, subject to the following 
conditions: 
 
1. This Special Use Permit shall allow for the installation of a meteorological tower, with a 
maximum height of 197 feet. 
 
2. The meteorological tower shall be e rected only in the location indicated on the approved site 
plan, except as may otherwise be approved by the Navajo County Public Works Department. 
 
3. Building permits are required for the meteorological tower and any accessory uses.  Any 
required permits shall be obtained prior to construction. 
 
4. A Floodplain Use Permit, if required, shall be obtained prior to issuance of any building permits. 
 
5. The meteorological tower foundation and all guy-wire footings shall be enclosed by a security 
fence with a maximum height of 7 feet (excluding barbed wire or cyclone wire).  Information 
regarding who to contact in the event of an emergency or any problems with the tower or its 
associated uses and structures shall be placed upon the fence.  The information shal l include a 
contact name, company name, and phone number for someone who can be reached 24 hours a 
day, 7 days a week. 
 
6. The meteorological tower shall include the installation of low-intensity, red blinking lighting for 
night-time visibility that conforms to FAA and FCC regulations.  The use of strobes or strobe -
type lighting is prohibited.  The meteorological tower shall also be painted in conformance with 
FAA and FCC requirements.

<!-- page 751 -->
7. Prior to acquiring a building permit, t he applicant shall work with the Arizona Game and Fish 
Department to design their tower in order to comply with the following requirements: 
 
a. Install Bird Flight Diverters (BFDs) at regular intervals along the full length of all outer 
meteorological tower guy wires. 
b. Install Aircraft Warning Markers (AWMs) near the tops of all outer meteorological 
tower guy wires. 
c. Paint the top of the meteorological tower orange and white. 
d. Locate the meteorological tower away from cliffs, canyons, water sources, and other 
wildlife-attracting features to the fullest extent possible. 
 
8. The applicant shall provide GPS locations of the final site of the meteorological tower to the 
Arizona Game and Fish Department, and to the Navajo County Public Works Department. 
 
9. The meteorological tower shall be located so that it will not fall onto an adjacent property nor 
another structure in case of failure. 
 
10. Prior to issuance of any building permits for the meteorological tower, the developer shall submit 
to the Navajo County Public Works Department information regarding the manufacturer of the 
tower, structural information, and information regarding who to contact in the event of an 
emergency or any problems with the tower. 
 
11. If the permitted Special Use is not utilized within a twenty-four (24) month period from the date 
of approval by the Board of Supervisors, this permit shall become null and void. 
 
12. Development and use of the site shall includ e efforts, consistent with Best Management 
Practices, to reduce and mitigate dust created by this project.  Efforts shall also be made to 
reduce the removal of vegetation during construction and use of the site and any roadways that 
provide access to the s ite.  Upon the removal of the meteorological tower and associated 
structures, the site and any roadways that provide access to the site shall be restored and re -
vegetated to their pre-disturbed/native condition by the applicant. 
 
13. Within six (6) months after the tower ceases to be used, the applicant, at their sole expense, shall 
remove the tower and any accessories from the site. 
 
14. This Special Use Permit and the rights granted herein shall expire sixty (60) months (5 years) 
from the issuance of a Certificate of Occupancy (C.O.O.), unless an extension is granted by the 
Board of Supervisors upon a recommendation by the Planning & Zoni ng Commission.  
Application for an extension shall be made no later than 90 days before the date of expiration.  
If timely application is made, the expiration shall be tolled until a final decision by the Board of 
Supervisors.

Dear   Mr.   Wynn:   
  
The  Arizona  Game  and  Fish  Department  (Department)  has  reviewed  the  proposed  installation  of               
five  meteorological  monitoring  towers  (MET  towers)  by  Pattern  Renewables  Development            
Company  2  LLC  (Pattern)  on  five  privately-owned  parcels  approximately  8.5  to  16.5  miles               
southwest  of  Holbrook,  Arizona  in  unincorporated  Navajo  County,  Arizona.  It  is  the              
Department’s  understanding  that  Pattern’s  proposed  installation  of  meteorological  test  towers  is             
part   of   a   larger   project   to   explore   and   potentially   develop   wind   resources   in   this   area.     
  
Under  Title  17  of  the  Arizona  Revised  Statutes,  the  Department,  by  and  through  the  Arizona                 
Game  and  Fish  Commission  (Commission),  has  jurisdictional  authority  and  public  trust             
responsibilities  for  management  of  the  state's  fish  and  wildlife  resources.  It  is  the  mission  of  the                  
Department  to  conserve  and  protect  Arizona’s  diverse  fish  and  wildlife  resources  and  manage  for                
safe,  compatible  outdoor  recreation  opportunities  for  current  and  future  generations.  Similarly,             
the  Department  recognizes  the  importance  of  planning  efforts  that  contribute  to  regional  and  the                
state’s  economic  growth  needs  and  opportunities  to  develop  renewable  energy  locations.  The              
Department  recognizes  that  appropriate  coordination,  proper  planning,  and  voluntary           
implementation  of  best  management  practices  allow  projects  to  be  developed  that  avoid,              
minimize,   or   mitigate   potential   impacts   to   wildlife   habitat   and   populations.     
  
The  Department  supports  the  development  of  wind  energy  as  a  source  of  clean  and  renewable                 
energy  and  believes  that  with  proper  placement  and  planning  the  benefits  of  wind  energy                
outweigh  the  potential  negative  effects  to  wildlife  populations.  As  identified  in  the  Department's               
" GUIDELINES  FOR  REDUCING  IMPACTS  TO  WILDLIFE  FROM  WIND  ENERGY           
DEVELOPMENT  IN  ARIZONA ”  ( Guidelines ),  primary  concerns  with  MET  towers  are  the             
potential  for  avian  and  bats  mortality  due  to  collisions  with  tower  guy-wires.  Another  potential                
issue  from  unmarked  towers  and  guy-wires  concerns  risk  to  Department  pilots  engaged  in               
low-altitude  wildlife  survey  flights  due  to  the  towers'  lack  of  visibility  from  the  air.  The                 
Department  appreciates  Pattern's  implementation  of  the  Department's  guidelines  to  minimize            
impacts  to  wildlife  and  risk  to  our  pilots.  To  further  protect  our  pilots,  the  Department  would  like                   
to  be  able  to  incorporate  the  GPS  coordinates  of  all  final  met  tower  locations  into  a  database  our                    
pilots  use  to  avoid  hazards.  Please  notify  the  Department  when  the  towers  are  erected  and  when

<!-- page 775 -->
Hot   Air   Wind   MET   Tower   Project   
February   16,   2021

they  are  taken  down  so  the  database  can  be  updated.  If  the  project  progresses,  the  Department                  
would  like  to  be  involved  in  the  planning/review  of  survey  designs,  provide  input  on  developing                 
best-management   practices,   and   post-construction   monitoring.   
  
The  Department  appreciates  Pattern’s  early  coordination  and  looks  forward  to  working             
proactively  and  collaboratively  to  develop  this  economically-important  facility  while  also            
minimizing  any  impacts  to  wildlife  during  development  and  operation  of  the  facility,  if  this                
project  does  move  forward.  Please  contact  me  at  623-236-7222  or   ACavalcant@azgfd.gov  if  you

approving/denying a Special Use Permit to construct and operate a 60 meter (approx. 197 foot)
meteorological tower on APN 110-07-001F, a portion of Township 16 North, Range 20 East,
Section 35 of the Gila and Salt River Meridian.
Background:
The proposed project is a 60 meter (approximately 197 foot) meteorological tower.  The applicant
is intending to use the tower to record meteorological conditions to research for a potential future
electrical generation project.  
The applicant for this project intends to have this tower constructed within a 2-year period and is
requesting a period of at least 5 years to operate the tower and collect data.
None of the structures and equipment on the site will be permanent.  Once site usage has
terminated, all of these structures and equipment will be removed and the site will be restored to
previous conditions.
This item was unanimously recommended for approval at the Planning and Zoning Commission
meeting held on February 18, 2021, subject to conditions outlined in the Staff Report and
Resolution for Approval.  These conditions include an amended version of conditions five (5),
which was recommended to be amended to state that fencing would only be necessary around
footings of the guy-wires and the foundation of the tower, as opposed to the entirety of the site.
Recommendation: 
Staff and the Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission recommend approval of the
Special Use Permit, subject to the conditions within the Staff Report.

BACKGROUND/PROJECT DESCRIPTION:  
 
The applicant is requesting Special Use Permit s to allow for the construction and operation of  five (5) 
different, 60 meter (approximately 197 foot) meteorological towers.  The location of the meteorological 
towers ranges from approximately 8.5 miles to 16.5 miles to the southwest of Holbrook. The applicant 
intends to use these towers to record met eorological conditions to research for a potential future 
electrical generation project. 
 
As far as construction of the towers, the applicant has described them as, “constructed of a guyed steel

<!-- page 780 -->
monopole structure approximately 60 meters tall.  Each structure would be installed within a cleared, 
approximately 0.03 -acre pad, and would occupy app roximately 2 acres when including the area 
encompassing the guy-wires.  For maximum safety, the towers would be painted orange and aviation 
white and include balls on the guy -wires.  To protect wildlife, bird flight diverters will be installed on 
all MET tower guy-wires at spaced intervals and towers are not located near wildlife attracting features 
(i.e. cliffs, canyons, water sources).” 
 
The applicant is planning to phase their installation of towers over a 2-year period from approval of the 
Special Use Permits.  In the applicant’s narrative, it has been noted that there is a request of a 5 -year 
operation period for these towers. 
 
The applicants will access these tower locations via State Route 377 and existing roadways that branch 
off to the locations. 
 
None of the structures and equipment on the sites will be permanent and will be removed from the site 
once usage has terminated.  The site will be required to be restored to the pre -disturbed/native state to 
the greatest extent possible upon completion of the usage of the meteorological tower. 
 
The applicant has reached out to the Arizona Game and Fish Department regarding these projects and 
Staff has been included within these interactions.  As of February 11th, 2021, no official letter has been 
received fr om the Arizona Game and Fish Department regarding conditions.  The Game and Fish 
Department has confirmed that they will have an official response to Staff prior to the scheduled 
Planning and Zoning Commission meeting on February 11th, 2021.  Staff has based conditions from the 
Game and Fish Department upon historical requests from this agency, which have been the same for all 
researched projects of this nature.  If the letter provides any new or changed conditions that are requested 
from Game and Fish, Sta ff will make sure to note this and change their official recommendation to 
reflect the alterations.  The typical conditions requested from Game and Fish, which have been included 
in Staff recommendations, are as follows: 
 
“To minimize collision risks to birds, bats, and Department personnel, the Department sees great benefit 
to MET tower construction by implementing the following measures: 
1. Install Bird Flight Diverters (BFDs) at regular intervals along the full length of all outer met 
tower guy wires to increase visibility of wires to birds. 
2. Install Aircraft Warning Markers (AWMs) near the tops of all outer met tower guy wires to 
increase visibility to pilots. 
3. Paint the tops of all met towers orange and white to increase visibility to pilots. 
4. Provide the Department with GPS coordinates of all final met tower locations. 
5. Locate MET towers away from cliffs, canyons, water sources, and other wildlife -attracting 
features to the fullest extent possible.” 
 
At the February 18, 2021 Planning and Zoning Commission meeting, all five of the meteorological 
towers were unanimously recommended for approval, provided that condition five (5) be amended to 
state fencing would only be necessary around footings of the guy-wires and the foundation of the tower 
and that the term of the Special Use Permits not exceed five (5) years.  Condition five has been amended 
to reflect this recommendation.  As there was already a recommendation for a five (5) year Special Use 
Permit term, condition fourteen (14) remains the same.  There were discussions regarding condition six 
(6) and lighting.  It was clarified that this condition only takes effect if lighting is required per FAA 
standards.

regarding who to contact in the event of an emergency or any problems with the tower or its 
associated uses and structures shall be placed upon the fence.  The information shal l include a 
contact name, company name, and phone number for someone who can be reached 24 hours a 
day, 7 days a week. 
 
6. The meteorological tower shall include the installation of low-intensity, red blinking lighting for 
night-time visibility that conforms to FAA and FCC regulations.  The use of strobes or strobe -
type lighting is prohibited.  The meteorological tower shall also be painted in conformance with 
FAA and FCC requirements.

Department to design their tower in order to comply with the following requirements: 
 
a. Install Bird Flight Diverters (BFDs) at regular intervals along the full length of all outer

b. Install Aircraft Warning Markers (AWMs) near the tops of all outer meteorological

February   16,   2021  
  
Mr.   Allen   Wynn

RE:   Hot   Air   Wind   MET   Tower   Project     
  
Dear   Mr.   Wynn:   
  
The  Arizona  Game  and  Fish  Department  (Department)  has  reviewed  the  proposed  installation  of               
five  meteorological  monitoring  towers  (MET  towers)  by  Pattern  Renewables  Development            
Company  2  LLC  (Pattern)  on  five  privately-owned  parcels  approximately  8.5  to  16.5  miles               
southwest  of  Holbrook,  Arizona  in  unincorporated  Navajo  County,  Arizona.  It  is  the              
Department’s  understanding  that  Pattern’s  proposed  installation  of  meteorological  test  towers  is             
part   of   a   larger   project   to   explore   and   potentially   develop   wind   resources   in   this   area.     
  
Under  Title  17  of  the  Arizona  Revised  Statutes,  the  Department,  by  and  through  the  Arizona                 
Game  and  Fish  Commission  (Commission),  has  jurisdictional  authority  and  public  trust             
responsibilities  for  management  of  the  state's  fish  and  wildlife  resources.  It  is  the  mission  of  the                  
Department  to  conserve  and  protect  Arizona’s  diverse  fish  and  wildlife  resources  and  manage  for                
safe,  compatible  outdoor  recreation  opportunities  for  current  and  future  generations.  Similarly,             
the  Department  recognizes  the  importance  of  planning  efforts  that  contribute  to  regional  and  the                
state’s  economic  growth  needs  and  opportunities  to  develop  renewable  energy  locations.  The              
Department  recognizes  that  appropriate  coordination,  proper  planning,  and  voluntary           
implementation  of  best  management  practices  allow  projects  to  be  developed  that  avoid,              
minimize,   or   mitigate   potential   impacts   to   wildlife   habitat   and   populations.     
  
The  Department  supports  the  development  of  wind  energy  as  a  source  of  clean  and  renewable                 
energy  and  believes  that  with  proper  placement  and  planning  the  benefits  of  wind  energy                
outweigh  the  potential  negative  effects  to  wildlife  populations.  As  identified  in  the  Department's               
" GUIDELINES  FOR  REDUCING  IMPACTS  TO  WILDLIFE  FROM  WIND  ENERGY           
DEVELOPMENT  IN  ARIZONA ”  ( Guidelines ),  primary  concerns  with  MET  towers  are  the             
potential  for  avian  and  bats  mortality  due  to  collisions  with  tower  guy-wires.  Another  potential                
issue  from  unmarked  towers  and  guy-wires  concerns  risk  to  Department  pilots  engaged  in               
low-altitude  wildlife  survey  flights  due  to  the  towers'  lack  of  visibility  from  the  air.  The                 
Department  appreciates  Pattern's  implementation  of  the  Department's  guidelines  to  minimize            
impacts  to  wildlife  and  risk  to  our  pilots.  To  further  protect  our  pilots,  the  Department  would  like                   
to  be  able  to  incorporate  the  GPS  coordinates  of  all  final  met  tower  locations  into  a  database  our                    
pilots  use  to  avoid  hazards.  Please  notify  the  Department  when  the  towers  are  erected  and  when

<!-- page 807 -->
Hot   Air   Wind   MET   Tower   Project   
February   16,   2021   
Page   2   of   2   
they  are  taken  down  so  the  database  can  be  updated.  If  the  project  progresses,  the  Department                  
would  like  to  be  involved  in  the  planning/review  of  survey  designs,  provide  input  on  developing                 
best-management   practices,   and   post-construction   monitoring.   
  
The  Department  appreciates  Pattern’s  early  coordination  and  looks  forward  to  working             
proactively  and  collaboratively  to  develop  this  economically-important  facility  while  also            
minimizing  any  impacts  to  wildlife  during  development  and  operation  of  the  facility,  if  this
